source.title: Ranking Deep Learning Generalization using Label Variation in Latent Geometry Graphs
source.authors: Carlos Lassance; Louis Béthune; Myriam Bontonou; M. Hamidouche; Vincent Gripon

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different measured property—label variation in latent geometry graphs—tracks generalization performance; it does not test the specific interventions or sharpness measure named in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports PGDL competition scores and rankings for its proposed measures. The flattened Table 2 does not support reliable assignment of its values to measures and task columns; no training-versus-test errors or per-network gaps are reported.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a latent-geometry label-variation score for predicting generalization. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or test any intervention or comparison specified in V1–V8. Citing Jiang et al. does not constitute a test of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present latent-geometry label variation as a proxy for generalization, report third place in PGDL, and call for deeper ablation to identify which components explain its performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses latent geometry graphs and label variation, sometimes with mixup, to predict generalization; it does not apply the listed interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that mixup and using the simpler VPM score improved balance between public and development sets; increasing the number of graphs improved VPM results on the public set. Final tasks used one graph, and the paper reports high variability across final tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed label-variation predictor ranked third in PGDL, with a final mean competition score of 9.99 and task scores ranging from 2.28 to 16.23. Its public/development performance depended on the score formulation, mixup and number of sampled graphs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label variation in latent geometry graphs can predict generalization rankings in the tested PGDL setting, with performance sensitive to predictor configuration and task.

record.problems: The authors state that a more in-depth ablation is needed. Final-task results had high variability; the number of graphs was reduced to one for the final submission. The flattened Table 2 prevents reliable recovery of its measure-by-task values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted. Competition scores in Table 2 are flattened beyond reliable assignment, and the stated ranking and qualitative claims do not report a train-test gap or a per-network result suitable for a row under the catalog criteria.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance with random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under controlled training budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout settings and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Competition scores evaluate the proposed predictor; they do not establish any listed version. Mixup augments inputs used to construct the predictor's graphs, rather than providing a controlled training intervention on the evaluated networks. No claim-relevant rows are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Width sweeps and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Large versus small batch size and training-budget effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
